questions.stem: A 68-year-old client had a basal cell carcinoma removed from the forearm by shave excision this morning. The site is covered with a pressure dressing. Which discharge instruction should the nurse include?
options: “Clean the site twice a day with hydrogen peroxide to prevent infection.”
“Leave the site uncovered so that a dry scab can form over the wound.”
“You can skip sunscreen on this arm now that the cancer has been removed.”
“After the first day, wash gently, then apply petrolatum and a clean bandage.”
optionRationales: Hydrogen peroxide is cytotoxic to fibroblasts and new epithelial cells and delays healing. Gentle soap and water is enough.
A dry scab slows the migration of epithelial cells. A moist, covered wound heals faster with less scarring.
A person who has had one basal cell carcinoma is at high risk for another skin cancer. Sun protection and regular skin checks must continue for life.

Correct. After the initial dressing is removed (usually 24–48 hours), gentle daily washing, a thin layer of petrolatum, and a clean bandage keep the wound moist and protected, which promotes healing and reduces scarring.
questions.rationale: Wounds left after skin cancer excision heal best in a clean, moist, covered environment. Teaching includes gentle daily cleansing, petrolatum and a bandage, avoiding harsh antiseptics, reporting signs of infection (spreading redness, warmth, purulent drainage, fever) or bleeding, and lifelong sun protection and skin surveillance because the risk of a new skin cancer is high.
questions.takeaway: After skin cancer excision: gentle wash, petrolatum, cover, and keep up sun protection for life.

A client at 24 weeks with blotchy brown patches on the forehead and upper lip
A client at 34 weeks with intense itching of the palms and soles and no rash
A client at 30 weeks with pink-purple streaks on the abdomen, hips, and breasts
optionRationales: Linea nigra is an expected hormonal hyperpigmentation of pregnancy.
Melasma (chloasma) is expected. Teach sun protection, since it darkens with UV exposure.

Correct. Generalized itching that is worst on the palms and soles in the third trimester, without a primary rash, suggests intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. It needs serum bile acids and LFTs and carries a risk of stillbirth.
Striae gravidarum are expected stretch marks from skin stretching and hormonal effects on collagen.
questions.rationale: Most pregnancy skin changes (linea nigra, melasma, striae, spider angiomas, mild pruritus, atopic eruption of pregnancy) are benign. Intense palm and sole itching late in pregnancy without a rash is the exception. It points to cholestasis, which threatens the fetus.
questions.takeaway: Late-pregnancy itching of the palms and soles with no rash = think cholestasis and report it.

Class III – Contaminated
Class IV – Dirty/Infected
optionRationales: Clean wounds have no inflammation and no entry into the GI, respiratory, genital, or urinary tract.
Clean-contaminated means controlled entry into a tract without infection, such as removing a non-inflamed appendix.
Contaminated covers fresh accidental wounds, major breaks in sterile technique, or GI spillage with non-purulent inflammation.
Correct. Existing clinical infection (pus) or perforated viscera makes the wound dirty/infected. The organisms were present before surgery, and the infection risk is highest.
questions.rationale: CDC wound class reflects contamination and predicts surgical site infection risk. Perforation and pus = Class IV Dirty/Infected. Expect antibiotics and possibly delayed primary closure.
questions.takeaway: Pus or perforation = Class IV dirty.

questions.stem: A client asks why the scraped knee from a bike fall healed without a scar but the deep cut from a glass injury left one. What is the best explanation by the nurse?
options: “The scrape was partial thickness, so the same tissue was able to grow back.”
“The scrape healed faster because it was an intentional, controlled wound.”
“The cut was a closed wound, so the tissue under it could not regenerate.”
“Scars form only when a wound becomes infected during the healing process.”
optionRationales: Correct. Partial-thickness wounds keep dermal appendages that regenerate epithelium with minimal scarring. Full-thickness wounds heal by connective tissue (scar) repair.
A bike fall is an unintentional wound, and intent does not decide scarring.
A cut through the skin is an open wound. Depth, not open vs closed, decides scarring.
Full-thickness wounds scar even without infection. Infection can make scarring worse.
questions.rationale: Depth decides healing: partial-thickness loss (epidermis ± part of dermis) regenerates, while full-thickness loss (all skin layers ± deeper) needs connective tissue repair and leaves a scar.
questions.takeaway: Partial-thickness regenerates. Full-thickness scars.

Hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL
WBC 8,200/mm³
Platelets 245,000/mm³
optionRationales: Correct. Albumin <3.5 g/dL indicates poor protein and nutritional status. It increases infection risk and delays collagen formation and wound healing.
This hemoglobin is normal and supports adequate oxygen delivery to tissues.
This WBC is within normal limits and shows adequate infection defense.
This platelet count is normal and supports hemostasis.
questions.rationale: Wound healing depends on adequate protein, oxygen (Hgb), immune defense (WBC), and clotting. Only the albumin is abnormal. The nurse should notify the provider and request a dietitian consult for a high-protein, high-calorie plan.
questions.takeaway: Albumin <3.5 g/dL = healing at risk.

questions.stem: A client with a healing leg wound has a prealbumin of 11 mg/dL and a poor appetite. Which dietary recommendations should the nurse make? Select all that apply.

Add citrus fruits and vegetables rich in vitamin C
Limit fluids to reduce wound drainage
Offer small, frequent meals and oral nutritional supplements
Follow a low-calorie diet to promote circulation
Take a high-dose zinc supplement daily even if zinc levels are normal
optionRationales: Correct. Protein supplies amino acids for collagen and tissue repair. Needs rise with wounds.
Correct. Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis.
Incorrect. Adequate hydration is needed for perfusion and tissue repair. Restricting fluids impairs healing.
Correct. Small, frequent meals and supplements increase total intake when appetite is poor.
Incorrect. Healing tissue needs more calories. Calorie restriction leads to breakdown of body protein.

Incorrect. Zinc supplementation helps healing only when a deficiency exists. Routine high doses are not recommended and can interfere with copper absorption. Food sources of zinc and vitamin A are encouraged instead.
questions.rationale: A prealbumin below about 15 mg/dL suggests recent protein malnutrition. Healing needs more calories, protein, vitamins A and C, and fluids. Small frequent meals, supplements, and a dietitian referral help when appetite is poor. Micronutrient supplements such as zinc are given for a documented deficiency, not routinely.
questions.takeaway: Wounds need calories, protein, vitamins A and C, zinc, and fluids.

“I won't donate blood while I'm taking this medication.”

Correct choice because the statement is wrong. Contraception must continue for 1 month after the last dose because isotretinoin is highly teratogenic.
This is correct. Depression and suicidal thoughts have been reported and must be reported right away.
questions.rationale: Isotretinoin causes severe birth defects and is available only through the iPLEDGE REMS program. Clients who can become pregnant need two forms of contraception from 1 month before through 1 month after therapy, plus pregnancy testing, no blood donation, and monitoring of mood, lipids, and liver function.
questions.takeaway: Isotretinoin: contraception from 1 month before until 1 month after.

questions.stem: The nurse is applying a prescribed topical corticosteroid cream to a client's eczematous plaques. Place the steps in the order the nurse should perform them.
options: Verify the order, identify the client with two identifiers, and perform hand hygiene
Put on clean gloves
Gently cleanse the area to remove the previous medication and pat dry
Apply a thin layer of cream, rubbing gently in the direction of hair growth
Leave the area uncovered unless an occlusive dressing is prescribed, then remove gloves and perform hand hygiene
questions.rationale: Safe topical application follows the rights of medication administration and hand hygiene. Gloves protect the nurse from absorbing the drug. Removing old medication prevents buildup. A thin layer rubbed in the direction of hair growth reduces folliculitis. Occlusion increases absorption and adverse effects (atrophy, systemic effects), so use it only when ordered.
questions.takeaway: Topical steroid: clean, thin layer, no occlusion unless ordered.

questions.stem: The nurse is assessing several newborns in the nursery. For each finding, indicate whether it is expected or unexpected (requires follow-up).
rows: Tiny white papules on the nose and chin of a 1-day-old
Blotchy red macules with pale yellow centers on the trunk of a 2-day-old
Blue-gray patches over the sacrum of an infant with dark skin
Yellow skin and sclera noted 12 hours after birth
A flat, dark-red port-wine stain over the forehead and eyelid
optionRationales: Expected. Milia are blocked sebaceous glands that resolve on their own.
Expected. Erythema toxicum is benign, appears at 24–72 hours, and needs no treatment.
Expected. Congenital dermal melanocytosis (Mongolian spots) is common in darker-skinned infants. Document it so it isn't mistaken for bruising.
Unexpected. Jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic (for example, hemolytic disease) and needs a bilirubin level and prompt evaluation.
Unexpected. A port-wine stain in the trigeminal (forehead/eyelid) area can be linked to Sturge-Weber syndrome (seizures, glaucoma) and needs evaluation.
questions.rationale: Normal newborn skin findings include vernix, milia, erythema toxicum, acrocyanosis, Mongolian spots, and stork bites. Jaundice before 24 hours and facial port-wine stains in the trigeminal distribution need follow-up.
questions.takeaway: Milia, erythema toxicum, and Mongolian spots are normal. Jaundice before 24 hours is not.

questions.stem: The RN is instructing a UAP caring for an 86-year-old client with thin, fragile skin and senile purpura on both forearms. Which instructions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Use a draw sheet with a second person to reposition the client in bed
Bathe with lukewarm water and a mild cleanser, then pat the skin dry
Dress the client in short sleeves so any new bruising is easy to see
Secure dressings with standard adhesive tape so they stay in place
Scrub the skin vigorously to stimulate circulation
Pad the bed rails and wheelchair arms
optionRationales: Correct. Lifting with a draw sheet prevents friction and shear, which cause skin tears.
Correct. Hot water and harsh soap strip the oils older skin can't replace. Pat, don't rub.
Incorrect. Long sleeves, pants, or limb protectors add a protective layer against bumps and skin tears. New bruising is checked during routine skin care, not by leaving fragile skin exposed.
Incorrect. Standard adhesive tape can tear fragile skin when removed. Use silicone tape, paper tape, or tubular/gauze retention instead.
Incorrect. Vigorous friction damages thin, fragile skin.
Correct. Padding prevents bumps that cause skin tears and purpura.
questions.rationale: Aging skin is thin and dry, with fragile vessels and less fat, which puts older adults at high risk for skin tears. Gentle bathing, lifting devices, padding, protective clothing, and avoiding adhesives protect tissue integrity. These routine care tasks can be delegated to a UAP with clear instructions.
questions.takeaway: Fragile older skin: lift, don't drag. Pat, don't rub. Pad, don't tape.
